name: Azaries Amnera
source:
Azaries (full name is Azaries Erandis Cirrus Amnera) – is a main character of Heralds of the Avirentes - Ch. 1 Wings of Change. Azaries shall be a key playable character for the most of walkthrough.

In Prologue, Azaries is a young 3 meters long silver purple-eyed om’verai with a long blonde hair and short face, with a spike on her nose. Azaries’ belly is covered with golden plates. Azaries’ head is decorated by 5 horns – 3 are situated on a forehead (1 short and 2 curved) and 2 straight ones below her eyes. An older Azaries from Chapter 1 is a 7-meters long[1] om’verai with a longer face. For some reason, Azaries’ eye color is an object of interest of some characters. Starting with Chapter 1, a chosen class affects Azaries’ appearance.

Azaries has a kind and friendly personality, she is always to land a helping paw to weaker ones. Azaries loves candies, though Azaries cares about her shape, clean scales and hair.

Azaries has a personality, similar to teens’ and youth’. A silver om’verai enjys reading adventure books, eating sweets and playing console videogames. Azaries is an “adventurer” who knows how to find adventures for her fifth assignment. Azaries does have a childhood problem with nightmares. Further changes of Azaries’ personality are directly depending on a player’s action during walkthrough.

Azaries is a young om’verai, the only daughter of Cyrus and Erandis, living in a small town of High Circles. Azaries’ dream is to leave her hometown and to release herself in a sphere, chosen by a player.

Mysterious stranger Akhellis sees Azaries one of those, capable to save Nanras from the coming disaster. Things are not that easy! A mysterious stranger shall show the path. What kind of secret lies behind Azaries’ purple eyes? Why ancient war mechanisms work in her paws? Why is local fauna so aggressive recently?

Azaries enjoys writing fanfics after books she read.
Azaries’ favorite dish is fried fathdogs’ legs.
A game will show up different scenes and dialogues depending on Azaries’ decisions to kill or to spare defeated foes.
